item.title: Keynote Speakers
item.description:
We are delighted to announce the first keynote speakers for Computational Humanities Research 2027 (CHR2027).

The keynote programme reflects CHR’s commitment to bringing together internationally recognised researchers whose work advances computational approaches to the humanities while fostering dialogue across disciplines. Further keynote speakers and lecture details will be announced in due course.

Katherine McDonough

Lancaster University (UK)

Katherine McDonough is a historian and digital humanist whose research explores the intersections of environmental history, digital history, and the history of climate and environmental knowledge. Her work combines computational methods with historical inquiry to investigate long-term environmental change, textual archives, and the circulation of knowledge across time and space.

item.title: Code of Conduct
item.description:
Purpose and scope

The organisers of the Computational Humanities Research conference are committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and accessible environment in which everyone is treated with fairness, dignity, and respect.

This Code of Conduct applies to speakers, session chairs, organisers, volunteers, attendees, exhibitors, and anyone else participating in CHR2027. It covers all conference-related activities, including sessions, workshops, social events, digital communications, and any online elements that may be offered.

item.title: Discover ARoS Art Museum with Free Voucher
item.description: As a participant in the upcoming CHR2024 conference, you have a unique opportunity to explore the renowned ARoS Art Museum, where art truly comes to life. We are excited to offer all attendees vouchers that can be used during your stay in Aarhus, giving you the chance to experience the museum’s extraordinary collections and exhibitions.

item.title: Keynote Lauren Klein
item.description:
About Lauren

We are happy to announce that Lauren Klein, Winship Distinguished Research Professor and Associate Professor in the departments of Quantitative Theory & Methods and English at Emory University, will give a keynote speech at the Computational Humanities Research 2024 Conference.

item.title: Keynote Leon Derczynski
item.description:
About Leon

We are happy to announce that Professor Leon Derczynski, principal research scientist in LLM Security at NVIDIA and prof in Natural Language Processing (NLP) at ITU Copenhagen (IT University of Copenhagen) will give a keynote speech at the Computational Humanities Research 2024 Conference in Aarhus, Denmark.

item.title: Past Events
item.description:
CHR2025

CHR2025 was a three-day conference held on December 10 to 12, 2025. The program committee and organizers accepted 97 papers, which have been published with the Anthology of Computers and the Humanities: https://anthology.ach.org/volumes/vol0003/. See https://2025.computational-humanities-research.org/ for more information about CHR2025.

CHR2024

CHR2024 was a three-day conference held on December 4 to 6, 2024. The program committee and organizers accepted 49 papers, which have been published with CEUR-WS: https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3834/. See https://2024.computational-humanities-research.org/ for more information about CHR2024.

item.title: Join the Community
item.description:
Want to stay in touch with the CHR community? Please sign up for the CHR mailing list! Via this list, the board will share important updates with all members, and it also enables community members to circulate relevant vacancies, calls, and other announcements.

item.title: Bursaries
item.description:
Digital Scholar will offer five bursaries of €500 each to support early-career researchers with limited financial resources or in precarious working positions who wish to present at CHR2027 in Manchester.

Call for Applications

The bursaries are intended to reduce participation costs, such as travel and accommodation, for early-career researchers who might otherwise be unable to attend. Applicants must have at least one accepted contribution (paper, poster, lightning talk, or workshop) in the CHR2027 programme.

item.title: Call for Papers
item.description:
In recent years, the arts and humanities have seen a significant increase in the use of computational, statistical, and mathematical approaches. This kind of research is distinguished by its reliance on formal methods and the development of explicit, computational models – ranging from quantitative and statistical techniques to broader computational methods for processing and analysing data, as well as theoretical reflections on these approaches.

The CHR conference seeks to be a venue where scholars can present and publish computational work while maintaining a strong connection to traditional humanities inquiry.

item.title: Campus Accessibility
item.description:
We want CHR2027 to be welcoming and accessible to everyone attending the conference. Detailed information about the accessibility of the conference buildings and rooms will be added once the programme and room allocation have been confirmed.

Access requirements and additional support

We are happy to provide additional services and support where possible. If you have any access requirements or need specific arrangements in order to participate in the conference, please let the local organisers know as far in advance as possible by emailing local@computational-humanities-research.org. This will give us the best opportunity to discuss your needs and make suitable arrangements.

item.title: CHR 2025 in Luxembourg
item.description:
The 6th edition of the Computational Humanities Research (CHR) conference will take place at the Luxembourg Centre for Contemporary and Digital History (C²DH) at the University of Luxembourg from 9 to 12 December 2025.

Renowned for its focus on providing a dedicated venue for presenting computational work that bridges formal methods and traditional inquiry in the arts and humanities, the CHR conference offers a platform to explore computational, statistical, and mathematical approaches, alongside theoretical reflections on these methods. We look forward to continuing our discussions in Luxembourg!

item.title: CHR Journal
item.description:
The Cambridge University Press journal Computational Humanities Research (CHR) is the official journal of the CHR Conference. CHR is an open access journal in the computational humanities, publishing transdisciplinary papers that are grounded in humanities research questions and use computational, quantitative methodologies to analyse humanities data in its various forms.

CHR publishes research that tackles big questions and solves problems pertaining to the humanities through advanced computational methods, contributing empirically to major theoretical, cultural, and historical inquiry. It seeks papers that spotlight quantitative and computational methods and applications, including the practical use and impact of computational techniques, in humanities research.

item.title: CHR2027 Review Guidelines
item.description:
If you notice any problems meeting the review deadline or with your assignments, or if you have any questions about EasyChair, please contact us as soon as possible.

Please note: If a submission violates template, anonymization, or reference requirements, do not proceed with review; contact the CHR2027 programme chairs.

Please also note that we assign a small number of community member and non-expert reviews in order to promote interdisciplinarity, diversity, and community engagement.

item.title: Diversity and Inclusion at CHR2024
item.description:
New initiatives, like the Anti-Discrimination Committee and reduced fees, reinforce the CHR2024 Conference’s commitment to accessibility and inclusivity, ensuring all participants feel valued and supported.

Since its inception five years ago, the Computational Humanities Research (CHR) Conference has developed into a prominent and well-regarded event, attracting researchers who apply computational methods across various humanities fields. This growth has enriched the CHR community, diversifying both the range of topics explored and the contributors involved.

item.title: Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
item.description:
CHR2027 is committed to creating a welcoming conference at which everyone is treated with fairness, dignity, and respect and has a genuine opportunity to participate. Our approach is informed by the University of Manchester’s commitment to an inclusive, diverse, and accessible environment and by the CHR Code of Conduct.

Our commitments

We aim to:

  • provide an environment free from discrimination, harassment, bullying, and victimisation;
  • respect participants’ identities, backgrounds, names, and pronouns;
  • consider accessibility and inclusion throughout the conference programme, venue arrangements, catering, and social activities;
  • listen to participants’ individual requirements rather than make assumptions about the support they need; and
  • respond to concerns fairly, sensitively, confidentially, and without retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith.

Inclusive participation

When registration opens, participants will be invited to tell us confidentially about access, dietary, religious, caring, or other requirements that may affect their participation. Providing this information will be optional. We will work with participants and the University to make reasonable arrangements wherever possible.

item.title: Vacancies in the CHR Board
item.description:
Looking to make an impact in Computational Humanities? The Society of Computational Humanities Research (SCHR) is recruiting an Early Career Representative and a Proceedings Officer to join its board. These volunteer roles are perfect opportunities to shape the field and support its growing community.

Apply by 21 February 2025!

Vacancy 1: Early Career Representative for the Society of Computational Humanities Research (SCHR)

The Society of Computational Humanities Research (SCHR) is seeking an Early Career Representative to join its board. This newly established role is dedicated to representing the interests of early career researchers within the Society. As Early Career Representative, you will act as a bridge between the Society and the early-career research Computational Humanities Research community, ensuring their perspectives are heard and their needs addressed. This is a remote volunteer position for a minimum of one year with the possibility of extension for another year. The estimated workload for this role includes bi-monthly meetings, and an average commitment of approximately one day of work per month, though this may vary throughout the year.
